messages:
maria-s: Hey team — ACME (acct: acme-prod) filed a streaming incident. They start an SSE session, receive ~300 tokens, then mid-stream the connection gets a 429 and the client reconnects. Customer reports they were charged for both partial streams (double-count) and wants root cause + repro steps. Attaching request ids.

sam-support: Thanks — can you paste the root request_id and the session_id? Also which SDK/curl they used? Any client logs?

maria-s: request_id: r_0a9b7c1f, session_id: s_acme_331. Customer repro steps (from their engineer):

1) curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-temp" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \"https://api.redwood.com/v1/stream?model=redwood-3b&stream=true&session=s_acme_331\"
2) client receives ~3 data events then: HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests (no Retry-After). Client code auto-retries with a refreshed token (sk-acme-rot1). Reconnect succeeds and emits remaining tokens.

Client log snippet:
```
[2026-02-12T14:02:12Z] SSE open (r_0a9b7c1f)
[2026-02-12T14:02:13Z] data: {"delta":"Hi"}
[2026-02-12T14:02:14Z] data: {"delta":"there"}
[2026-02-12T14:02:15Z] HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
[2026-02-12T14:02:15Z] reconnect with sk-acme-rot1
[2026-02-12T14:02:15Z] SSE open (r_0a9b7c1f-retry)
```
\nmaria-s: Customer says billing shows two separate token entries tied to two different API keys, total > expected.

paolo-eng: cc @maria-s — looks like this is the classic mid-stream auth rotation + 429 interaction. Quick notes: our accounting attribution is per-HTTP connection and increments the token counter when we finalize chunks from that connection. If a connection is terminated with a non-OK (e.g., 429) and the client immediately reconnects with a rotated key, both connections can be accounted separately. That can appear as double-billing for one logical chat session.

paolo-eng: Repro I ran locally: start SSE with key A, simulate a forced 429 from the rate limiter after N tokens, then reconnect with key B. Server logs show two usage rows: one for key A (tokens until 429) and one for key B (tokens after reconnect).

paolo-eng: Example server-side log excerpt:
```
[2026-02-12T14:02:15Z] request_id=r_0a9b7c1f key=sk-acme-temp status=429 tokens_reported=78
[2026-02-12T14:02:15Z] request_id=r_0a9b7c1f-retry key=sk-acme-rot1 status=200 tokens_reported=220
```
\npaolo-eng: Two important details: 1) our billing export ties usage rows to the API key in the HTTP Authorization header that established the connection. 2) We don't currently have an automatic merge for sessions that reuse the same request_id but different keys.

nina-billing: caught this in invoice reconciliation yesterday — when customers rotate keys mid-session for short-lived tokens we see split lines. For enterprise accounts we sometimes reconcile and merge, but for self-serve billing the portal shows separate lines. We should avoid double-counting from normal retry flows.

sam-support: Actionable asks for triage:
- Confirm whether the 429 was due to per-key quota exhaustion or global account throttling.
- Check whether Retry-After header should be returned for mid-stream 429s to discourage immediate reconnect.
- Determine mitigation: server-side merge, attribute retries to original key when request_id matches, or require idempotency token.

paolo-eng: Quick debug steps I suggest for support + eng:
1) From customer, capture full raw HTTP traces including headers for both connections. Need Authorization header values (obfuscated is fine) and request_id.
2) Check rate-limit scopes in the returned 429 (our rate-limiter currently sets X-RateLimit-Scope: "key" or "account").
3) If 429 lacks Retry-After, that's a bug — add Retry-After with a short backoff for streaming 429 paths.
4) Short-term workaround: ask customer to avoid rotating keys mid-SSE. Use a single long-lived key for the session or attach a session-level idempotency token header (X-Session-Id) so we can attribute reconnects to the same session.

maria-s: customer provided obfuscated headers for r_0a9b7c1f, will paste in a DM. They do rotate ephemeral keys frequently (security practice).

nina-billing: If customer wants immediate remediation we can apply a manual billing merge for that invoice, but we should fix platform-side to not surface split usage for benign reconnects. Opening a billing ticket now.

support-bot: Support ticket created: INC-2026-4482 referencing r_0a9b7c1f. Escalation level: P2.

paolo-eng: I'll add a tiny server change: when we see a reconnect within 5s with same request_id/session-id, attribute tokens to the earliest successful key and mark the earlier 429 as "transient" for billing (not incrementing separate invoice lines). Will open PR and link here.

maria-s: Thanks — I'll share the reproducible curl and the customer's raw traces in the ticket. Customer is asking for ETA on fix and a one-off invoice merge.

sam-support: ETA: quick fix to return Retry-After on streaming 429s — low-risk, can ship in next sprint (3 business days). Billing merge — manual today, process paperwork. Keep me posted. :+1:

maria-s: Adding customer success and closing initial loop. I'll post updates to INC-2026-4482.
